messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: control-plane deps high 5xx rate -> paging SREs :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Alert details: service=control-plane, symptom=5xx spike and timeouts, affected endpoints=[/v1/auth/*, /v1/org/lookup, /v1/config], current window: 3m, error_rate=11.8%
maria (oncall-sre): acked, I'm on it. pulling metrics + runbook now — linking runbook: <https://runbooks.internal/redwood/control-deps-5xx>
maria (oncall-sre): initial quick check: ingress shows surge of 503s from gateway -> upstream 502/504 from auth-proxy cluster. p95 latency for auth lookup = 6.2s (baseline 120ms)
kevin (sre): taking pager for next 30m. maria, can you capture hostnames and recent deploys? I'll start tracing RPC fanout.
maria (oncall-sre): copying logs: ran `kubectl -n controlplane logs deploy/auth-proxy --tail=200` and saw repetitive errors: `ERR dial tcp x.x.x.x:5432: i/o timeout` and a bunch of `context deadline exceeded`
ashley (platform): FYI we rolled a small change to org-lookup client pool yesterday 02:10 UTC (change id: cfg-4579). Not yet associated but flagging it.
tanvi (eng): i'm on the org-lookup service. checking DB pool metrics and connection counts.
kevin (sre): flipping to live tail of gateway logs and adding temporary error-rate dashboard filter
kevin (sre): gateway shows spike of 502/504 with increasing upstream retry attempts. Here's a snippet from the gateway: ```[2026-03-14T17:04:22Z] GET /v1/auth/token 502 upstream reset by peer id=auth-proxy-3 attempts=2 latency=1.3s```
luis (support): I'm getting a few customer reports about failed auth leading to UI errors — flagging high-priority customers in case we need direct comms
maria (oncall-sre): mitigation idea: temporarily route traffic away from auth-proxy pool to fallback instances in us-west-2. Can platform do region failover?
ashley (platform): we have warm backup pool in us-west-2 but it requires enabling a routing flag `enable-regional-fallback` and a small DNS/traffic switch. I'll prepare the switch and coordinate.
kevin (sre): while that is prepped, can we reduce concurrency from gateway to auth-proxy to avoid exhausting DB connections? set `proxy.max_inflight=50` for auth route.
tanvi (eng): DB shows connection count jumped from 120 -> 950 concurrent connections after a surge of auth requests at 16:57 UTC. Connection waiters also spiked. Query latency increased accordingly. Suspect connection pool mis-sizing + retry storm.
maria (oncall-sre): applying temporary gateway rate limit and backoff: `curl -X POST https://gateway/api/config -d '{"routes":{"/v1/auth":{"max_inflight":50,"retry":false}}}'` — applied. Watching.
kevin (sre): reduced retry config to avoid exacerbating DB load. Also disabled a recent client-side aggressive retry header that was being passed from edge.
ashley (platform): ready to flip regional fallback. I'll flip in 2m and monitor. prep command: ```platform-fallback switch --service auth --to-region us-west-2 --dry-run=false```
deploy-bot: Deploy `cfg-4579` (org-lookup client pool change) was applied 2026-03-13T02:10:41Z to cluster controlplane-prod-1
maria (oncall-sre): noting correlation: timestamps line up with low-traffic period but the error spike appears later after a billing job at 16:55 caused burst of background jobs. adding to timeline.
kevin (sre): regional fallback started by ashley. traffic shift=~30% to us-west-2. beginning to see auth errors decrease on primary pool. error_rate -> 4.1% after 4m
tanvi (eng): investigating cfg-4579 client pool defaults — looks like max_open_conns not set, connecting attempts create new connections until DB limit hit. patch incoming to set sane defaults and connection queueing.
maria (oncall-sre): confirming customer impact: about 18 customer sessions affected, some failing login and org lookup for ~10min window. support notified.
luis (support): posting status on status.redwood.com and pinging top-10 customers via email template.
kevin (sre): mitigation summary so far: 1) throttled gateway concurrency 2) disabled retries 3) switched partial traffic to fallback region 4) rolled temporary DB connection guard lines in org-lookup client (hotfix queued)
tanvi (eng): hotfix prepared: `org-lookup: set max_idle=50 max_open=200 conn_wait=true` — will rollout to a single canary pod now. command: `kubectl -n controlplane set image deploy/org-lookup org-lookup=org-lookup:hotfix-20260314-canary`
maria (oncall-sre): canary shows stable connections and reduced connection churn. metrics look good. initiating gradual rollout.
kevin (sre): monitoring error rate and latencies. p95 auth latency trending down from 6.2s -> 280ms over 12m. overall 5xx down to 0.6%
ashley (platform): reverted routing flag after 25m; traffic normalized. documented the fallback steps in the runbook.
maria (oncall-sre): declaring mitigation in progress. preparing post-incident notes and timeline. please keep any relevant logs or snippets here.
luis (support): customer comms: initial status posted, follow-up note scheduled for 1h with root-cause summary and mitigation steps.
kevin (sre): next actions: postmortem owner? assigning tanvi as eng lead for RCA, ashley for platform follow-up (routing automation), maria for incident timeline and ops notes.
tanvi (eng): taking RCA. preliminary root cause: client pool config defaulted to unbounded open connections combined with a background billing job spike -> DB exhausted connections -> upstream timeouts -> gateway 5xx + retry amplification.
maria (oncall-sre): final status: service degraded window: 16:57–17:19 UTC, error_rate peak 11.8%, from 17:08 mitigations reduced errors steadily, service recovered 17:19 UTC.
kevin (sre): closing pager. leaving thread open for RCA docs and follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
maria (oncall-sre): adding checklist items: ensure client pool defaults set in config templates, add alert for DB connection count > 70% of max, implement safe defaults in CI for client libraries.
tanvi (eng): will produce RCA doc and timeline in /confluence/incidents/1845023456-rca and link back here.
kevin (sre): thanks all — good coordination.
ashley (platform): one more note: we'll add a quick-button in console for emergency regional fallback to shave 90s off next time.
luis (support): I'll follow up with customers and close comms when postmortem is ready.
kevin (sre): last check: logs archived, capture saved to s3://incident-archives/1845023456.tar.gz
maria (oncall-sre): handoff: I am handing back to the normal oncall rotation. If anything pops up ping `#incidents` or escalate to kevin.
kevin (sre): thread closed but keeping for post-incident edits. thanks everyone.
